shots.line: She asked for three birds from every house... and burned an entire city with them.
shots.scene: night, moon, red horizon: a cloud of burning birds streams from the siege camp over the palisade into a wooden town on a rocky hill — the camera flies with them; at 'burned an entire city' every roof bursts into flame

shots.line: Kiev, nine forty-five. A tribe called the Drevlians murders Prince Igor. Then they make a fatal mistake.
shots.scene: golden sunset over Kiev on the Dnieper; the camera glides across the river into a birch forest where fur-hatted Drevlians encircle Prince Igor; their prince Mal steps forward grinning

shots.line: They send men to marry his widow... Olga. She greets them with honor.
shots.scene: sunset on the Dnieper: the Drevlian longboat full of envoys rows towards the Kiev bank; the camera tracks it until Olga, waiting with her guards, smiles graciously

shots.line: And buries them alive... in their own boat.
shots.scene: the envoys still sit in their boat — now deep in a pit; Olga's men shovel earth over them under a blood-red sunset

shots.line: She asks for their noblest men next. They are led to a bathhouse. The doors are locked. Then... the fire.
shots.scene: sunset yard: Olga smiles 'send me your noblest men'; the camera follows Drevlian nobles into a steaming log bathhouse; a soldier bars the door; flames climb the straw roof

shots.line: At her husband's funeral feast, the Drevlians drink... until her soldiers draw their swords.
shots.scene: sunset at Igor's burial mound: long tables, Drevlians drink and laugh; the camera follows Olga walking along the tables; at her signal her men draw their swords — red flash

shots.line: Then she besieges their city, Iskorosten. For a whole year... it will not fall. So Olga makes an offer.
shots.scene: sunset reveal: Iskorosten on its granite hill above the river, ringed by Olga's striped tents and banners; a calendar spins through a year; the camera descends to Olga's red tent where a townsman kneels

shots.line: "I want no more revenge. Only a small gift." "Three pigeons and three sparrows... from every house." The city laughs. And pays.
shots.scene: close on Olga at her tent, sweetly: no more revenge — only three pigeons and three sparrows from every house (icons pop in); the camera swings to the town gate where laughing townsfolk hand over wicker cages

shots.line: That night, her men tie burning sulfur to every bird... and set them free. The birds fly home. Back to their nests. Under the straw roofs.
shots.scene: moonlit night in the camp: soldiers at campfires tie smoking sulfur to the birds; on 'set them free' a cloud of burning birds explodes upward and the camera flies with them over the palisade down onto the straw roofs

shots.line: Every house catches fire at once. The woman who did this... was later declared a saint.
shots.scene: every house of Iskorosten burns at once under a red sky; the camera sweeps around and lands behind Olga standing on a rise, her silhouette against the inferno
a golden icon: Saint Olga with a halo — the flames behind her
